notes: בַּת הַיַּעֲנָה → *ostrich* is retained as one indivisible rendering under rule 30, with the separately segmented article taking the written *the* beside it, exactly as in the דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים example; the head is the lexeme-carrying יַעֲנָה.

*night hawk* heads on *hawk*, which the ASV writes alone for נֵץ later in the verse (rule 31's tie-break), while *sea mew* heads on *mew* under the ordinary subtraction test — the two are decided by what the ASV writes, not by position.
